label: Thomas Aquinas, Sententia libri…: There is a mover that moves something, is moved in no respect of…
interpretation: Aquinas on 1072b4-10. What is moved by generation, growth or alteration is otherwise and otherwise in something intrinsic (substance, quantity, quality); what is moved in place is otherwise only in place, not in substance (n. 12). 'Cum igitur primum mobile habeat se aliter et aliter secundum locum, et non secundum substantiam, oportet quod primum movens, quod est immobile et semper actu ens, nullo modo possit aliter et aliter se habere, quia non potest moveri': it would be moved above all by the first motion, local and circular, but it is not moved by the motion by which it moves, so it cannot be moved in any way and cannot be otherwise in any way (n. 13). The existence of a first mover not moved is presupposed (n. 1, 'cum ostensum sit, quod sit primum movens non motum'). Read as STMT-SOME-UNMOVED-MOVER-CANNOT-BE-OTHERWISE: some mover moved in no respect of change and in act in being cannot be otherwise in any respect of change. The respects of change are those n. 12 names (substance, quantity, quality, place; DEF-RESPECT-OF-CHANGE); because 'nullo modo' is argued from 'non potest moveri' through the kinds of motion, it is not read beyond them. Aquinas says more of the mover (immobile, 'non potest moveri', 'semper actu ens'); the statement keeps only that it is not moved in a respect of change and is in act in being, which his words entail. Aquinas' mover moves 'sicut desiderabile' (n. 1-3); reading the case's MovesIn to include that is the choice recorded in DISAMB-MOTION. The necessity of n. 13-15 (said of the first motion, ex fine) is not used.
